provenance_correction: CORRECTED 2026-08-06T15:30Z by claude-opus-5/orcha. This file and T387's close note originally said the row's console had died (it had never recorded a heartbeat since dispatch 2026-08-06T00:24:23Z). That inference was WRONG: the console was alive and relaunched the identical defective command at 16:46:12 local, which I found still spinning 40 minutes later (10:50 CPU, same infinite loop at t387_budget.zig:718-719 confirmed by a second sample(1)) and reaped. So the row had TWO concurrent runs of the same hung binary, and 'never beat a heartbeat' meant only that the console never exported MANAGENT_TASK_ID — it did NOT mean the console was dead. The lesson for liveness readings: absence of heartbeats proves absence of instrumentation, not absence of a console. The salvaged readings and the u6 diagnosis are unaffected.

readings.role: SEEDED CONTROL — proves the back-edge detector fires on the unbudgeted graph

Measured: 135,494 back edges in the unbudgeted 3x3 graph, 0 with the budget at B=8, at both 3x3 and 4x3. The control firing is what makes the two zeros readable.
what_this_does_NOT_support: Bellman consistency under budget-from-here. Proven by sample(1): 2,554/2,554 stack samples at :718-719 after 14h02m elapsed / 836 CPU-minutes / 880 KB RSS / no output file. Do not cite this file as evidence about the Bellman identity. The at-risk class T386 measured is 80/2,748 at 3x3 and 496/51,318 at 4x3; nothing has been compared against those denominators.

new_rows.claim: **Bounding total captures makes the move graph acyclic — measured, with the control firing.** Every cycle in Go must contain a capture (returning to a position requires the stone count to come back down, and only captures do that), so a capture budget should remove every back edge. Readings at B=8: **135,494 back edges in the unbudgeted 3x3 graph** (the seeded control, proving the back-edge detector is sensitive), **0 back edges at 3x3 over 423,922 states**, **0 back edges at 4x3 over 10,636,928 states**. A DAG has a unique minimax value, so the bracket cannot exist under the budget. This is the structural half of the operator's capture-budget line and it reaches what superko cannot: the absurd clump-die-repeat games never repeat a position, so superko never bites them. **EXPLICIT NON-CLAIM:** this says NOTHING about Bellman consistency under budget-from-here. That reading was T387's other half and it NEVER RAN — src/t387_budget.zig:717-719 is an infinite loop (bitpos declared u6 against a `while (bitpos < 64)` guard its own type cannot falsify; += 1 wraps rather than traps under the -O ReleaseFast tools/runner forces), proven by sample(1) at 2,554/2,554 stack samples after 14h02m and 836 CPU-minutes with 880 KB RSS and no output. Nothing has been compared against T386's at-risk denominators (80/2,748 at 3x3, 496/51,318 at 4x3). T397 owns the fix and that reading. **PROVENANCE CAVEAT:** these three readings were salvaged from uncommitted /tmp by the Orchestrator after the row failed; they are the instrument's own self-report with no independent re-derivation, hence MEASUREMENT.
